raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Deterministic inference picks a CUDA-only attention backend on Intel XPU. With no `--attention-backend`, `_deterministic_attention_backend` falls through the SM100/SM120 check to `fa3`, whose factory asserts `SM>=80 and SM<=90`. `get_device_capability()` returns `(None, None)` on XPU, so the assert fires and the server dies during startup:

```
Attention backend not specified. Falling back to 'fa3' for deterministic inference.
...
AssertionError: FlashAttention v3 Backend requires SM>=80 and SM<=90.
```

Every deterministic run on XPU that does not name a backend is affected, including a plain `--enable-deterministic-inference` launch. `intel_xpu` is already in `DETERMINISTIC_ATTENTION_BACKEND_CHOICES`; nothing selected it.

## Modifications

- `arg_groups/overrides.py`: resolve the deterministic fallback to `intel_xpu` on XPU. The branch only runs when `attention_backend is None`, so an explicitly requested backend is untouched.
- `test/registered/unit/test_model_overrides.py`: cover both directions - the XPU fallback resolves to an XPU-capable backend, and an explicit backend is left alone. The first case fails on pre-fix code (verified), the second passes before and after.

## Accuracy Tests

Intel Arc Pro B60, `sgl-kernel-xpu` built from source.

`test/registered/cuda_graph/breakable/test_bcg_with_lora.py` - unmodified by this PR, and the test that surfaced the bug, since it enables deterministic inference without naming a backend. Before: every case errored at server launch on the fa3 assert. After: **12/12 pass** (`TestBCGLoRACsgmv` 6/6, `TestBCGLoRATriton` 6/6, ~2.5 min per class on one card).

Logs confirm the fix took effect and the test is not passing vacuously: each of the four servers logs `Falling back to 'intel_xpu' for deterministic inference`, and each class records 10 prefill batches served by the breakable CUDA graph (`cuda graph: True`), so the graph-vs-eager prompt-logprob comparison really ran through the graph path.

New unit cases: 2 passed; 1 of the 2 fails when the fix is reverted.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable - startup-path config resolution only, no effect on steady-state inference.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

files.patch:
@@ -1079,7 +1079,10 @@ def _deterministic_attention_backend(view: Any) -> dict:
 
     if view.attention_backend is None:
         # User didn't specify attention backend, fallback based on GPU architecture
-        if get_platform().is_sm100 or get_platform().is_sm120:
+        if get_platform().is_xpu:
+            # fa3 and flashinfer have no XPU kernels.
+            backend = "intel_xpu"
+        elif get_platform().is_sm100 or get_platform().is_sm120:
             # Blackwell and newer architectures
             if _deterministic_is_deepseek_model(view):
                 # fallback to triton for DeepSeek models because flashinfer

@@ -4004,5 +4004,41 @@ def test_explicit_choices_are_not_replaced(self, _mock_model_type):
         self.assertEqual(envs.SGLANG_MM_FEATURE_CACHE_MB.get(), 2048)
 
 
+class TestDeterministicAttentionBackendOnXpu(unittest.TestCase):
+    """The deterministic fallback must not hand XPU a CUDA-only backend.
+
+    fa3 asserts on the device's SM version, so an XPU server that only asked
+    for --enable-deterministic-inference dies at launch rather than falling
+    back. The explicit-backend case guards the other direction: the platform
+    branch must not override a backend the user named.
+    """
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _view(attention_backend):
+        return SimpleNamespace(
+            enable_deterministic_inference=True,
+            attention_backend=attention_backend,
+            model_path="Qwen/Qwen3-4B",
+        )
+
+    def test_xpu_fallback_is_an_xpu_backend(self):
+        with patch.object(
+            overrides_module, "get_platform", return_value=SimpleNamespace(is_xpu=True)
+        ):
+            updates = overrides_module._deterministic_attention_backend(
+                self._view(None)
+            )
+        self.assertEqual(updates, {"attention_backend": "intel_xpu"})
+
+    def test_xpu_keeps_explicit_backend(self):
+        with patch.object(
+            overrides_module, "get_platform", return_value=SimpleNamespace(is_xpu=True)
+        ):
+            updates = overrides_module._deterministic_attention_backend(
+                self._view("triton")
+            )
+        self.assertEqual(updates, {})
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()
